signal: Today’s strongest signal is that AI engineering is shifting from generic generation toward closed-loop, verifier-aware systems: agents are orchestrating formal proofs and hardware tuning, small side models can estimate failure before execution, alternative decoding architectures are compressing generation steps, and local-model runtimes are plugging directly into mainstream agent front ends.

stories.title: Anthropic says Claude produced the first complete computer-checked proof of Fermat’s Last Theorem
stories.summary: Anthropic says Claude worked largely autonomously for 11 days to produce an end-to-end Lean formalization of Fermat’s Last Theorem. The effort generated about 13 million lines of Lean and proved 30,300 theorems, with 29,500 used in the final proof. Early multi-agent attempts lost track of project state; the successful run used Prove2Me to maintain a theorem-dependency DAG, separate statements from proofs, and make intermediate results searchable and reusable. Anthropic says the final proof was checked by Lean and matched Mathlib’s statement of FLT.
stories.whyItMatters: The standout result is not merely mathematical: it shows how long-horizon agents can make progress when the environment supplies objective verification, explicit dependency state, and parallelizable work units. For AI engineering, this is a strong pattern for research and software agents—externalize the task graph, let deterministic tools reject invalid work, and make intermediate artifacts reusable instead of asking one context window to remember an entire project.
stories.attention: Very high — verifier-backed multi-agent systems are crossing from toy proofs into extremely large formal artifacts

stories.title: Google’s MaxKernel uses multi-agent search to beat hand-tuned TPU kernels on aggregate
stories.summary: MaxKernel is a Google and Google DeepMind multi-agent system for TPU kernel engineering that combines planning, implementation, compilation repair, testing, autotuning, and hardware profiling. On 50 JaxBench tasks, its parallel-search mode compiled and passed correctness checks on all 50 and achieved a 1.58× geometric-mean speedup over the JAX/XLA references. On eight workloads with expert-written Pallas kernels, the paper reports a 2.32× geometric-mean speedup for MaxKernel parallel search versus 2.02× for the hand-tuned references.
stories.whyItMatters: This is a concrete example of AI-for-AI infrastructure optimization where the model is only one component of a closed feedback loop. Compiler errors, numerical tests, profiler traces, snapshots, and graph search provide the signals that make low-level optimization reliable. The same design principle applies beyond TPUs: agents become much more valuable when they can iterate against hard measurements rather than prose-only self-critique.
stories.attention: Very high — autonomous agents are becoming competitive with expert performance engineering when backed by compiler and profiler feedback

stories.title: A small draft model can predict coding-agent failures before expensive actions execute
stories.summary: Speculative Uncertainty (SU) estimates the failure likelihood of a black-box coding agent using only its generated tokens. A smaller open-weight draft model scores the already-produced reasoning and action spans in one forward pass, and the resulting features are calibrated against a verifiable objective. In experiments with Qwen3-Coder-480B and Claude 3.5 Sonnet agents, a pre-execution veto gate reduced execution error rate by 6–8 percentage points and token cost by 14–19%, while transferring to out-of-distribution benchmarks without retraining.
stories.whyItMatters: Production agents need a control signal between 'the model wants to do this' and 'the system should pay for or execute it.' SU is attractive because that signal does not require access to the frontier model’s logits or weights. A cheap side model can become a risk/cost gate that routes uncertain cases to tests, stronger models, human review, or additional reasoning before external effects occur.
stories.attention: Very high — black-box agent reliability can gain a practical pre-execution confidence layer without provider internals

stories.title: PlaidQ compresses diffusion-based code generation from 512 denoising steps to 16 — and even one
stories.summary: PlaidQ is a 0.7B continuous diffusion language model that repurposes a pretrained autoregressive model as a bidirectional denoiser over continuous token embeddings. The authors distill a 512-step teacher into much shorter generation trajectories: a 16-step student reaches 31.78 pass@10 on HumanEval and 40.49 on MBPP+, exceeding the same teacher sampled for 512 steps. A one-step paired-trajectory student reaches 7.07 pass@1 on HumanEval and can already produce functionally correct programs.
stories.whyItMatters: Autoregressive token-by-token decoding is not the only viable execution model for code generation. If continuous diffusion can retain useful quality under aggressive trajectory distillation, it opens another quality/latency trade-off surface and potentially more parallel generation. The result is early and small-scale, but it is worth tracking because inference architecture—not just model size—may become a major lever for agent latency.
stories.attention: High — continuous diffusion is showing a credible path toward very few-step language generation

stories.title: Ollama 0.34 RC1 lets ChatGPT Desktop call local open models directly
stories.summary: Ollama’s 0.34.0 RC1 adds the ability to use Ollama-hosted models directly from ChatGPT Desktop, with setup exposed through the Ollama app on macOS. The pre-release also improves structured-output performance on Apple Silicon, adds OpenAI-compatible client tool search and response compaction, and fixes image handling through compacted responses.
stories.whyItMatters: Local inference becomes more useful when it plugs into mainstream agent surfaces instead of requiring a separate UI. For teams building local-plus-cloud routing, this is another sign that OpenAI-compatible interfaces and tool semantics are becoming a portability layer: inexpensive or private work can stay local while the front end and higher-level workflow remain unchanged. Because this is an RC, it belongs in experimentation rather than a production rollout.
stories.attention: High — local models are moving behind familiar agent interfaces instead of living in separate developer sandboxes

takeaway: Build around explicit feedback and replaceable runtimes. Preserve dependency graphs and execution state, couple agents to deterministic verifiers and profilers, gate costly actions with cheap predictive signals, benchmark new generation architectures end to end, and keep local/cloud model boundaries swappable behind compatible interfaces.
